title: NIST Handbook 162: NIST MEP Cybersecurity Self-Assessment Handbook for Assessing NIST SP 800-171 (withdrawn 2022)

history.reason: Source fetched and read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

reliability: US government (NIST MEP) document; MEP funds and promotes the assistance it describes, so it has an interest in presenting need for that assistance.
findings: The cover notice states Handbook 162 was published November 20, 2017, and withdrawn September 23, 2022, superseded by NIST SP 800-171A and DoD guidance.
The handbook states NIST SP 800-171 "assumes that small manufacturers currently have IT infrastructures in place, and it is not necessary to develop or acquire new systems to handle CUI."

The handbook states "Small manufacturers may not have the necessary organizational structure or resources to satisfy every security requirement" and that alternative but equally effective measures are acceptable.

The handbook states conducting security control assessments "can be challenging, and resource-intensive" and expects the business owner, COO, IT manager, security manager and plant managers to work together on an assessment.
The handbook states that in 2016 the MEP National Network had 51 centers and connected with 25,445 manufacturers.
limitations: Withdrawn; keyed to SP 800-171 Rev. 1 and pre-CMMC; current requirements differ.
A how-to guide; it contains no measurement of how many small manufacturers meet or miss the requirements.
